chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Barmaki, from Ali ibn Abbas al-Kharadhini, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Jafar al-Jafari, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

It was mentioned in his presence that a group of people claim that God, Blessed and Exalted, descends to the nearest heaven. So he said: Indeed God does not descend, nor does He need to descend. Rather, His sight regarding the near and the far is the same — a close thing does not become far from Him, nor does a distant thing come near to Him. He has no need of anything; rather, all things are in need of Him. He is the Possessor of Bounty. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

As for the statement of those who describe Him that He, Blessed and Exalted, descends — only one who attributes deficiency or increase to Him would say that; for every moving thing needs something to move it or something it moves with. So whoever entertains false conjectures about God is destroyed.

Therefore, be cautious regarding His attributes lest you impose a limit upon Him, defining Him by deficiency or increase, or causing movement or motion, or decline, or descent, or rising, or sitting — for God is far more Majestic and Mighty than the descriptions of the describers, the characterizations of the characterizers, and the imaginations of the imaginers. Put your trust in the Mighty, the Merciful, Who sees you when you stand (for prayer) and your prostrations among those who prostrate.

key_terms.الْوَاصِفِينَ: The describers — those who apply human physical attributes to God, which the Imam condemns as attributing deficiency or increase
key_terms.تَوَهُّمِ الْمُتَوَهِّمِينَ: The imaginations of the imaginers — human mental constructs that fall short of grasping the divine reality
key_terms.ذُو الطَّوْلِ: Possessor of Bounty/Excellence — a divine epithet indicating inexhaustible power and grace
key_terms.مَنْظَرُهُ: His sight/vision — refers to God's omniscient perception that is equally encompassing of near and far, negating physical directionality

ai.seo_question: Does God descend to the lowest heaven according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him), the seventh Imam, refutes the anthropomorphic claim that God physically descends to the lowest heaven — a belief held by certain groups of his era. The Imam articulates a sophisticated theology of divine transcendence: God's perception encompasses all things equally regardless of proximity; He needs nothing and is needed by all; and every movement implies dependency on a mover, which cannot be attributed to God. The hadith concludes with a Quranic citation (26:218-219), urging reliance on the All-Seeing, Merciful God who transcends all human description and imagination.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al Barmakky, from Ali Bin Abbas Al Kharaziny, from Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘It was mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence that a group of people are claiming that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High<sup>azwj</sup> Descends to the sky of the earth’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not descend, nor is He<sup>azwj</sup> needy to that He<sup>azwj</sup> should descend. But rather His<sup>azwj</sup> Viewing regarding the near and the far is the same. A close by (thing) is not far from Him<sup>azwj</sup>, nor is a remote (thing) close to Him, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is not needy to anything, but He<sup>azwj</sup> is what (things) are needy to. He<sup>azwj</sup> is with the Power. There is no god except Him<sup>azwj</sup>, the Mighty, the Wise’.

As for the words of the describers, that He<sup>azwj</sup> the Blessed and High Descends, so rather they are saying that for the one who is linked to the decrease of increase, and every mover is needy to the one who moves it, or moves with it. So the one who thinks of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with the conjectures is destroyed.

Therefore, be cautions with regards to Hisazwj Attributes from that you should be pausing to Himazwj upon a limitation, limiting Himazwj by a decrease or an increase, or moving or being moved, or decline, or descent, or advancement, or failure, for Allahazwj is more Majestic and Mightier than the description of the describers, and characteristics of the characterisers, and the imaginations of the imaginers; and rely upon the Mighty, the Wise who Sees you when you are standing (for the Salat), and your turnings among the prostrators’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah has narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il al-Barmaki from Ali ibn ‘Abbass al-Kharazini from al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Ya‘qub ibn Ja‘far al-Ja‘fari, from abu Ibrahim (a.s.) Who has said the following.

“A people was mentioned, before the Imam (a.s.), who believed that Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, comes down to the sky above the earth.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Allah does not come down and He does not need to come down. His sight for near and far is the same. Near does not become far for Him and far does not become near for Him. He does not become needy for any thing but all things need Him and He is generous. There is no Lord except Him. He is Most Majestic and All-wise.

The statement that says Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, comes down to the sky over the earth can only come from those who consider Him to decrease or increase (in size). Besides, all moving objects need something to move it or move because of it. Whoever thinks of Allah as such has caused his own destruction.

Be very careful about the attributes of Allah to have a belief about them that would limit Him through increase or reduction, moving or being moved, removal or His coming down, standing up or sitting down. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, is far from being described by those who would like to describe Him or being characterized by those who do so or pictured in imagination. Have trust in Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Merciful Who sees you when you get up and when you change positions during prostration.”
